references.text: Isaiah describes Sheol (the realm of the dead) as receiving the dead, which corresponds to the rich man's stay in Hades. [ref:Isa 14:9-11|Isaiah 14:9-11]
Job describes the realm of the dead as a land of darkness and the shadow of death, providing background for the concept of Hades as a place of torment. [ref:Job 10:21-22|Job 10:21-22]
The wicked shall return to the realm of the dead – a basis for the idea that the rich man ends up in Hades. [ref:Ps 9:18|Psalms 9:18]
Peter quotes Psalm 16:10 about Hades (the realm of the dead) in his Pentecost sermon, using the same Greek word (ᾅδης) that Luke uses here. [ref:Acts 2:27|Acts 2:27]
Death and Hades give back the dead at the final judgment, confirming Hades as a temporary holding place for the dead. [ref:Rev 20:13-14|Revelation 20:13-14]
Abraham's role in the parable connects to the promise that Abraham himself would depart in peace – in contrast to the rich man's suffering. [ref:Gen 15:15|Genesis 15:15]

Jesus speaks of many sitting at the table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, while the children of the kingdom are cast out – a parallel motif to the rich man seeing Abraham from afar. [ref:Matt 8:11-12|Matthew 8:11-12]

Jesus speaks of weeping and gnashing of teeth when one sees Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the prophets in God's kingdom but is shut out – a close parallel to the rich man's situation. [ref:Luke 13:28|Luke 13:28]
The preceding verse tells that Lazarus was carried by angels to Abraham's bosom, directly contrasting the rich man's fate in Hades. [ref:Luke 16:22|Luke 16:22]
The continuation of the parable elaborates on the torments in Hades and the great chasm between the two places, completing the picture of the rich man's suffering. [ref:Luke 16:24-26|Luke 16:24-26]
Peter refers to the spirits in "guard" (φυλακή), shedding light on the concept of a holding place for the dead similar to the Hades motif in Luke. [ref:1 Pet 3:19|1 Peter 3:19]
Christ holds the keys to death and Hades, showing his authority over the place where the rich man is located. [ref:Rev 1:18|Revelation 1:18]
